name: EV Route Planning
description: Models a logistics network as cities and charging sites joined by road segments, alongside a fleet of electric vehicles described by battery, efficiency and charging limits. Answers which vehicles can cover a given lane, what a route looks like once charging stops are part of the plan, and which places sit beyond reach of any charger.

n:0.label: Geo
n:0.description: A place on the network that is not a charging site — a city, depot or delivery point. Deliberately carries no label in common with a charging site, since the spec allows a node only one primary label, so any traversal meaning 'any location' must name both labels explicitly or it will silently plan routes that never charge.

name.description: Name of the place, and its identifier on the network. Expected to be unique across the whole network rather than within a region. e.g. `Paris`.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees on WGS 84, positive northwards. Used for straight-line distance filters that prune candidates before a traversal; it is not the distance a vehicle drives, which is carried on the road segment. e.g. `48.8566`.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees on WGS 84, positive eastwards. e.g. `2.3522`.

region.description: Administrative region the place sits in, used to group and summarise coverage rather than to route. e.g. `Ile-de-France`.

n:1.label: ChargingStation
n:1.description: A site where vehicles can charge, sitting on the road network as a place in its own right. Shares no label with other locations, so a route that must be able to charge has to traverse both labels explicitly.

name.description: Name of the charging site, and its identifier on the network. e.g. `CS-A1-01`.

lat.description: Latitude in decimal degrees on WGS 84, positive northwards. e.g. `49.7953`.

lon.description: Longitude in decimal degrees on WGS 84, positive eastwards. e.g. `2.7256`.

region.description: Administrative region the site sits in, used to summarise charging capacity and coverage by area. e.g. `Hauts-de-France`.

operator.description: Network operator running the site. Expected to matter for access and tariffs rather than for routing. e.g. `ElectraRoute`.

power_kw.description: Maximum power the site can deliver to a single vehicle, in kilowatts. The power a given vehicle actually receives is the lesser of this and that vehicle's own charging limit, so this is a ceiling rather than a delivered rate. e.g. `350.0`.

n:2.label: Car
n:2.description: A vehicle in the fleet, described by the battery and efficiency figures a route plan needs. Carries no connection to the network: a vehicle is not positioned on the graph, but supplies the energy model a traversal is evaluated against.

id.description: Identifier for the vehicle in the fleet. e.g. `EV-001`.

model.description: Manufacturer's model name for the vehicle. Descriptive only; the energy model reads the numeric properties, never this. e.g. `Corvia eVan 60`.

vehicle_class.description: Category of vehicle, used to group the fleet when comparing what different classes can serve. e.g. `Light Van`.

battery_capacity_kwh.description: Usable battery capacity in kilowatt-hours. Expected to be the usable figure rather than the nominal pack size, since range is computed directly from it. e.g. `60.0`.

efficiency_kwh_per_km.description: Energy consumed per kilometre driven, in kilowatt-hours per kilometre — a consumption rate, so a higher number means a less efficient vehicle. Treated as constant, with no allowance for load, gradient, weather or speed. e.g. `0.24`.

max_charge_power_kw.description: Highest charging power the vehicle can accept, in kilowatts. Caps what it draws from a site however powerful that site is; a plan that ignores this cap produces charging stops shorter than the fleet can achieve. e.g. `90.0`.

current_soc_percent.description: Current battery state of charge as a percentage of `battery_capacity_kwh`, from 0 to 100. A snapshot of the vehicle now, and the starting state a route is evaluated from, not a static attribute. e.g. `38.0`.

r:0.description: A road segment between two places on the network, neither of them a charging site. Stored once per segment and expected to be traversed undirected: the stored direction is an artefact of how the row was written, not a one-way restriction, and reverse segments are deliberately not created. A place may be joined to several others, or to none.

road_ref.description: Designation of the road the segment belongs to, as signed. Several segments may share one designation. e.g. `A1`.

road_class.description: Class of road, from the network's own four-tier vocabulary — `Motorway`, `Express`, `Trunk` and `Local` — in descending order of speed. e.g. `Motorway`.

distance_km.description: Driving distance along the segment in kilometres. This, not the straight-line distance between coordinates, is what energy consumption is computed from. e.g. `112.7`.

free_flow_speed_kph.description: Speed in kilometres per hour expected on the segment when traffic is light — the off-peak case. e.g. `130`.

peak_speed_kph.description: Speed in kilometres per hour expected on the segment at peak traffic. Expected to be at or below the free-flow speed; choosing between the two is how a plan accounts for time of day. e.g. `95`.

r:1.description: A road segment joining a place to a charging site — the approach that makes the site reachable. Stored once per segment and expected to be traversed undirected, so this and the segment definition written from a site to a place are two halves of one convention rather than a pair of one-way roads. A place may reach several sites, or none.

road_ref.description: Designation of the road the segment belongs to, as signed. e.g. `A1`.

road_class.description: Class of road, from the network's own four-tier vocabulary — `Motorway`, `Express`, `Trunk` and `Local` — in descending order of speed. e.g. `Express`.

distance_km.description: Driving distance along the segment in kilometres, and the basis for the energy cost of detouring to charge. e.g. `105.8`.

free_flow_speed_kph.description: Speed in kilometres per hour expected on the segment when traffic is light. e.g. `130`.

peak_speed_kph.description: Speed in kilometres per hour expected on the segment at peak traffic. e.g. `105`.

r:2.description: A road segment joining a charging site back to a place — the continuation after a charging stop. Stored once per segment and expected to be traversed undirected. Not every site carries one, so its absence means only that no onward segment was recorded, never that a site is a dead end.

road_ref.description: Designation of the road the segment belongs to, as signed. e.g. `A1`.

road_class.description: Class of road, from the network's own four-tier vocabulary — `Motorway`, `Express`, `Trunk` and `Local` — in descending order of speed. e.g. `Express`.

distance_km.description: Driving distance along the segment in kilometres. e.g. `119.2`.

free_flow_speed_kph.description: Speed in kilometres per hour expected on the segment when traffic is light. e.g. `130`.

peak_speed_kph.description: Speed in kilometres per hour expected on the segment at peak traffic. e.g. `105`.

r:3.description: A charging option at a site, modelled as a self-loop so that a route can pass through a charging stop without leaving the site. One of these per tier the site offers, so a site carries several in parallel and they are distinguished by `tier` rather than by endpoint. Every site is expected to offer at least one.

tier.description: Name of the charging option, from the site's own vocabulary — a short `top-up` stop against a longer `full` charge. Distinguishes the parallel options at one site. e.g. `top-up`.

time_in_minutes.description: Dwell time the option represents, in minutes — how long the vehicle stands at the site. Combined with delivered power it gives the energy gained, and it is what a route's elapsed time accumulates. e.g. `15`.

power_kw.description: Power offered by this option in kilowatts. The vehicle receives the lesser of this and its own `max_charge_power_kw`, so energy gained is that lesser figure applied over the dwell time, never this figure alone. e.g. `350.0`.
